title: QBR concise facilitator pocket script & prep checklist
body:
Purpose: Quick, portable facilitation script and pre-meeting checklist for recurring QBRs. Designed for 30–60 minute executive or technical QBRs. Use as a pocket guide on the call and as a prep checklist 48–72 hours beforehand.

Top-level structure (30–60 min):
- 1) Welcome & outcome (2–3 min): quick recap of meeting purpose, who owns follow-ups, and the desired decision(s).
- 2) Business context & goals (5–8 min): customer updates, product/usage trends that matter to their KPIs.
- 3) Health snapshot (5–7 min): adoption metrics, latency/cost anomalies, support tickets & SLAs.
- 4) Initiatives & roadmap alignment (8–12 min): what we shipped, what’s planned, opportunities where Redwood can lower cost / latency.
- 5) Renewal & expansion signals (5 min): renewal timeline, seats/commits, blockers, recommended options.
- 6) Risks & escalation (3–5 min): unresolved issues and immediate mitigations.
- 7) Decisions, next steps, owners (2–3 min): confirm actions, owners, and dates.
- 8) Parking lot + close (1–2 min): capture items for follow-up, thank attendees.

Facilitator script (concise lines to read/adapt):
- Intro: “Thanks everyone for joining. We’ll run through a concise set of health signals, product alignment, and proposed next steps — goal is to leave with 2 clear decisions or follow-ups.”
- Transition to health: “Quick snapshot: adoption, any performance regressions, and support items that might affect your rollout.”  (If there’s a live dashboard, drop link and say: “I’ll share the dashboard — feel free to call out anything you want to dig into.”)
- On roadmap ask: “Based on your top priority, we recommend 1) test dedupe caching on high-throughput routes, 2) try a 4-bit quantized model variant for non-production workloads. Would you like a short pilot for either?”
- On renewal: “Your renewal is targeted for YYYY-MM-DD. Based on current usage projections we recommend Tier X or a committed capacity model Y — I’ll follow up with a short TCO and migration checklist.”
- Closing: “Confirming next steps: I’ll send the meeting notes and owners within 24 hours. If anything urgent, escalate to the SRE on-call or your CSM.”

Pre-meeting checklist (48–72 hours before):
- Confirm attendees and roles (decision maker + technical contact + finance if renewal imminent).
- Send pre-read with 1-page health snapshot, key asks, and proposed decisions.
- Pull latest metrics and attach: token spend by route, p50/p95 latency, error rate, top support tickets.
- Validate live demo requirements (env, creds, recording permission).
- Check quota/limits and any freesample credits that might be needed for demos.
- Prepare one slide with renewal options (current, step-up, committed-reserved).
- Create a short pilot proposal for any recommended experiments (scope, duration, success metrics).

Tech & logistics checklist (day of):
- Test meeting link and screen share, confirm presenter can share dashboard.
- Ensure recording enabled if customer OK.
- Load the metrics dashboard and the exact time window being discussed.
- Have direct Slack/phone to SRE or engineering owner in case a live troubleshooting demo is needed.

Renewal & expansion quick signals (what to surface live):
- Renew early signal: consistent year-over-year growth in monthly tokens + expansion of routes.
- Risk signal: sudden spike in p95 latency that persists > 48 hours or repeated throttled requests.
- Expansion opportunity: >3 teams using separate API keys and no dedicated capacity in place.

Escalation script (if call turns into incident):
- Acknowledge: “We hear the impact. We’re invoking a targeted triage: immediate owner is SRE x, engineering lead y, CSM z will coordinate customer comms.”
- Time-box next steps and commit to cadence: “We’ll follow up with a 60-min triage summary and a 24-hour remediation plan.”

Post-meeting deliverables (within 24–48 hours):
- Send meeting notes with decisions, owners, due dates.
- Attach updated health snapshot and the renewal option slide.
- If pilot agreed: send scope doc + first-week checklist + metrics to collect.
- Create follow-up Jira/Linear tickets and link to meeting notes.

Templates & short snippets to paste into emails/slack:
- Invite pre-read note: “Attached one-page snapshot for our QBR. Please review the health metrics and add any agenda items you want to discuss.”
- Follow-up note: “Thanks for today. Actions: 1) Owner — deliverable — due date. Next check-in: [date].”
- Renewal nudge 30/14/7 days: short cadence reminders with clear ask (e.g., choose tier, confirm PO).

Unresolved questions / To consider:
- Should we standardize a single health metric card for all QBRs (tokens, p95, errors, active routes)? Proposal: yes, keep to 4 metrics to keep calls short.
- Do we include pricing sensitivity bands in the same slide as product recommendations? (trade-off: clarity vs negotiation risk)

Notes to facilitator (informal):
- Keep the call customer-led — let them speak first on priorities. Use the script only as guardrails.
- If the customer is timeboxed, move decisions to a quick poll at minute 50 and capture in follow-up.
- Use the parking lot for anything tactical; avoid getting pulled into PoC implementation detail on the QBR call.

Decision log (template line to paste into notes):
- Decision: [short description] | Owner: [name] | Due: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Impact: [rev/ops/risk]

Quick references (links to internal templates / dashboards you should attach):
- Health dashboard (attach): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/customer-health?org=<<org-id>>&window=30d
- Renewal pricing matrix (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Renewal+Pricing+Matrix
- Pilot scope template (github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/customer-playbooks/tree/main/pilot-scopes

Version notes: created as a compact facilitator pocket guide for CS reps running short QBRs. Keep this doc pinned to the customer record and update with the most recent dashboard link before each QBR.

—— END ——
